chk_problem.poster_evidence: Roof construction, maintenance, installation, and inspection expose workers to significant slipping and falling risks. Many roof tasks are also physically demanding and repetitive, providing strong motivation for robotic assistance.

chk_setup.label: accurate

A Unitree Go2 running software version 1.4.4 was evaluated in three core skills: balancing on increasing inclines, performing get-up and lie-down sequences, and walking uphill. chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: The measured friction coefficient was 1.144 ± 0.1299 on flat tile sections and 1.430 ± 0.1298 on curved sections.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately states the measured friction coefficients, matching draft (b).

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: The critical angle for balanced standing was 27.58° ± 0.72°. Failure was primarily caused by automatic limb repositioning following foot slippage or atypical joint configurations. Get-up and lie-down motions succeeded only up to 11° in head-up and head-down orientations and 7° sideways.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster accurately states the critical standing angle and the get-up/lie-down success limits, matching draft (a).

chk_baseline.reason: The poster establishes the baseline performance of the Unitree Go2 robot with standard ball feet on the roof test rig, matching draft (b).

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Without significant modification, the Unitree Go2 was not suited for operation in roof environments.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately concludes that unmodified quadrupeds are not suited for safe operation in roof environments.
